title: decision-table
description: A rule as a table: one column per condition, one row per case, the outcome and the line that decides it. A row whose cell is missing shows an empty cell (“empty”), a row without an outcome “undefined”, and two rows that match the same case with different outcomes are flagged as contradicting each other. Each row with an anchor is content-checked: the anchored line must contain `literal`; a row with an anchor and no `literal`, or whose literal is not on the line, is shown as inferred. Not rendered when `rows` is empty.

outcomeLabel.description: Heading of the outcome column; defaults to “Outcome”.

id.description: Part id, unique in the block; a route step can focus it.

when.description: Condition id → the value in this row (`"≤ 14"`, `"yes"`). `"*"` means any value; leave a condition out for an empty cell.

outcome.description: What the rule decides; leave it out when the code decides nothing for this case.

literal.description: The condition or threshold exactly as written in code (`days <= 14`); the anchored line must contain it.

anchor.description: The line that decides this row.

note.description: One line shown under the row.

when.description: Only the cells that changed: condition id → old value; the other cells keep their current value.

outcome.description: Old outcome; "" when the code decided nothing for this case before.

literal.description: Old literal; the base anchor's line must contain it.

anchor.description: Into the base repo; checked against `before.literal`, or the old row is shown as inferred in Before. A changed `before.literal` without `before.anchor` is shown as inferred, with no code chip.
